'''''Pellaea rotundifolia''''', the '''button fern''', is a [[species]] of [[fern]] [[endemism|endemic]] to [[New Zealand]], where it grows in scrub and forests.<ref name=EGF/> It is also a popular [[garden]] plant (in zones 8 and 9) and [[house plant]], tolerating low temperatures but not freezing.<ref name=RHSPF/>

''Pellaea rotundifolia'' is a compact, [[evergreen]] fern that can have more than 30 pairs of round, dark-green, leathery pinnae on fronds up to {{cvt|18|in}} in length.<ref name=EGF>Olsen, Sue. Encyclopedia of Garden Ferns. 2007.</ref> The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''rotundifolia'' means "round-leaved".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

==Cultivation==
It needs acidic and well-drained soil; it does not appreciate the moist, humid conditions that most ferns require so does well with minimal watering.<ref name=EGF/>

This plant has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHSPF>{{cite web 
|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/12410/i-Pellaea-rotundifolia-i/Details |title=RHS Plantfinder - ''Pellaea rotundifolia''
 |accessdate=18 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=75 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=21 April 2018}}</ref>
